nodes.name: Get live resources
nodes.notes: Live resources only. Already-dead rows are skipped: they were checked, they failed, and re-fetching them weekly costs requests to tell us what we know. A human replacing the URL is what brings a row back.

nodes.name: Mark dead
nodes.notes: Sets dead + http_status. The row is kept, never deleted: study_plans reference resources by id, so deleting one would break every plan that already links to it.

fieldValues.fieldValue: ={{ $json.url }} returned {{ $json.http_status }}{{ $json.error ? ' (' + $json.error + ')' : '' }}. Hidden from the catalog until a replacement is found.

nodes.name: Log it for a human
nodes.notes: The row is already hidden by this point. This is the trail, so a dead link is something someone can go replace rather than something that silently vanished.

nodes.name: Record healthy check
nodes.notes: Writes http_status only. Note this also un-deads a link that came back: a 404 that turns into a 200 next week means the provider moved it back, and it should return to the catalog on its own.
